title: Spinalonga and Plaka
body: Today’s plan: boat to Spinalonga, then Plaka beach next door. Photos still to come.

title: South road to Elounda
body: Big Crete day on the south road. Down from the Rethymno side through Spili, along the south coast past Chora Sfakion and Ierapetra, then north to Kato Elounda. Photos still to come — this one’s the track for now. Morning surprise: a tabby already inside on the tiles. Dinner at Rakomelo Cretan Cuisine booked the old way: a handshake, nothing written down. Roadside stop: Julia hit our favorite store — a fig tree in Demati. Stopped at the Armeni necropolis — chamber tombs and a walk down the dromos. A melon truck in Asimi nearly stole the show. At Amiras, the memorial for those executed on 14 Sep 1943. Elounda evening: Mythos at Alikes, pebbles table by the water, then Rakomelo for the handshake dinner.

title: Georgioupolis day
body: Out of Douliana toward the coast: Kefalas for a rock swim and a bay full of cats, then Georgioupolis until the wind said enough. Lunch by the water — souvlaki, shrimp, Mythos — and the house dessert at Arkadi. Afternoon inland to Alikampos for vines and a barrel table in the shade, then soft landing in Vryses with ducks under the trees. Back at the stay we caught a cat burglar in the doorway. No valuables missing.

title: Almyrida
body: A beach day out of Douliana. Almyrida was the assignment: a still bay, white houses on the hill, and a long look at whether one of those might be a DDIC house. In the water a giant sea turtle came over to say hi. No pictures. Just memories of an old friend. Then Tsunami for Mythos and Greek junkfood pizza. After lunch we took the inland roads through Kokkino Chorio and Drapanos and came home to the village pool.

title: Over the mountains
body: Packed up Paleochora and drove north through Selino, the western foothills of the Lefka Ori — the White Mountains. Julia took a million and one pictures of the goats in the road at Seliniotikos Gyros — we waited, they inspected the asphalt, then we kept going. A stop at Manousakis Winery in Vatolakkos, then the drop toward the gulf. Keys at the BnB. Raki on the table, and last light over the village. Dinner at Ηλιοστάσι (Heliostasi): a huge Cretan salad, a mixed grill that delivered, creamy tzatziki, and me on raki with the bottle.

title: Sea day
body: West to Elafonissi for pink sand and a long swim — water so clear it looked edited. Later we found Gialiskari: pebble beach, a waist-deep wade, a school of little silver fish under the surface. Back in Paleochora, gin and tonics at Livikon Day to Night with the mountains across the bay. Dinner at Caravella — calamari, souvlaki, the whole steam-table parade — then watermelon and something sweet with raki on the rocks.

title: Cheers
body: Two frappés by the harbour. Yia mas. Drove west through Kissamos, then south over the mountains to Paleochora. Lunch at I Platia in Kandanos — spicy meatballs, the best. Evening stroll through a village that feels half fishing town, half Hollywood set. Dinner at Romeiko Wine & Deli: two reds and a shared board in the courtyard.

title: Saturday market
body: Saturday in Chania is the market. Grapes by the crate, onions by the pile, smoke off a street grill. The best cheap feast we know. Lunch at Το Σουβλάκι Όπως Παλιά. Best gyros in town, or a close second. More frappés by the harbour Dinner at TAMAM: dakos and fava, wine, braised octopus, lamb kabobs. Excellent. Stumbled into the Chania film festival. Full moon. It's not Greece without a protest.

title: Captain
body: He took the wheel. She took the bow. We rented a boat and borrowed the Mediterranean for a morning. Cave stop on Agii Theodori (Άγιοι Θεόδωροι). Tonight: the best seafood in town. Later, The Botanist. Aged Long Island iced tea — no Coke needed. We'll be back. Then the fort, floodlit.

title: Coffee to beer, and then some
body: From coffee to beer, same table, same view. We hadn't moved. Then the harbour lit up like a set, Ta Kalamakia fed us the best souvlaki in town, and we chased it with pomegranate juice and loukoumades. Walking the old town after that. Gotta love Crete.

title: Frappé by the harbour
body: First proper morning in Chania. Two frappés and cold water from the White Mountains at Neoria Fish Tavern, Venetian harbour behind us. Worth every delayed flight.

title: Keys in the door
body: Twenty-eight hours door to door, and every flight found a way to run late. We still made it. Pi Suite in Chania is ours for the night — bags down, lights low. Kalinihta from Crete.

title: Made the connection
body: The Burbank hop ran an hour late. We had an hour and a half on the ground at SFO and we used every minute of it — through the terminal at a run, onto the next plane with nothing to spare. Seats found. Breath caught. Next stop, Greece.

title: DDIC at Burbank
body: We made it to Hollywood Burbank Airport. Currently parked at Guy Fieri’s Kitchen + Bar Express with a couple of Space Dust IPAs — official Day Drinkers in California business before the long haul. Next stop: Crete. Wheels up soon. Καλή πτήση to us.

title: The plan, as booked
body: Five days out. We leave from Burbank on the 24th and land in Chania late on the 25th. Crete first — Chania, Paleochora, Douliana, Elounda, and Heraklion — before a morning ferry to Santorini on the 9th and on to Athens on the 12th. Home on the 17th. We’ll fill this in from the road.
